correctness.rationale: Edge differences form the zero-sum hyperplane and the Lipschitz norm is precisely the maximum of edge slopes, since paths bound all pairwise slopes and every edge is shortest. Changing coordinates gives max(|u|+|w|,(|v|+|w|)/t). Duality preserves the real Euclidean distance, and swapping u,v with a scalar realizes inversion of t. For t≥1 sign averaging preserves the quadratic sandwich and removes off-diagonal entries without raising distortion. On the unit norm body the maximal diagonal energy occurs at |w|=0 or 1: the upper corner energy a(1-z)^2+b(t-z)^2+cz^2 is convex. The reverse squared norm has exact Cauchy–Schwarz maxima 1/a+1/c and (1/b+1/c)/t². Normalize the reverse maximum to 1; at each h=1/c in (0,1) the smallest feasible a=1/(1-h), b=1/(t²-h) minimize the forward maximum. The two branches then strictly increase and decrease respectively. Their difference has numerator −(2t+1)(h−t)(h−t/(2t+1)) over h(1−h)(t²−h); only the second root is admissible, also at t=1. It follows that the displayed Q is optimal and the squared distance is 3−2(t−1)/((t+1)(2t−1)). Its derivative has sign t−2, giving the two reciprocal unique minima with squared value 25/9 and the uniform and degenerate limits 3. The displayed Q is in dual coordinates for t≥1, with t<1 handled by the swap/scaling. Frozen check.py is an exact rational finite check, not a continuum proof; independently verified contact candidates and off-optimum controls at five ratios with Fraction, replay python3 /workspace/branches/independent_finite_checks.py (check 2).

value.rationale: The four-cycle is the first cyclic transport example beyond trees and the alternating weights are a natural one-parameter deformation retaining opposite-edge symmetry. The exact optimum supplies a nonmonotone contrast with the cube endpoint and a one-defect plateau, identifies the precise best deformation, and produces the sharp quadratic comparison. General norm equivalences do not answer these questions.
